page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Add and subtract 1 to split it
steps.margin_note: First mark. Adding and subtracting 1 is the method. Rationalising with a² + ab + b² instead is an equally valid route and earns the same mark.
lines: At x = 0 the numerator is 1 − 1 = 0 and the denominator is 0, so the form is 0/0.
Add and subtract 1 in the numerator:
In the second part put t = −x; as x → 0, t → 0, and (1 − ∛(1 − x))/x = (∛(1 + t) − 1)/t

recall.must_convey: That adding and subtracting 1 splits the expression into two copies of the standard limit ((1 + x)ⁿ − 1)/x.
accept: add and subtract one so each cube root stands beside its own one
split it into two standard limits
put t equals minus x in the second part
okati add chesi okati subtract chesi rendu standard limits ga split cheyyali
use one plus x to the power n minus one over x

steps.why: Substitution gives the indeterminate form 0/0. Adding and subtracting 1 turns the expression into two copies of the standard limit lim(x → 0) ((1 + x)ⁿ − 1)/x = n.
common_mistakes: Writing ∛(1 + x) − ∛(1 − x) = ∛(2x); a cube root does not split across a difference.
Losing the sign at t = −x, which makes the two halves cancel and gives 0.
steps.memory_tip: Add and subtract 1 so that each cube root stands beside its own 1.

steps.label: Apply the standard limit with n = 1/3
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Box 2/3. Checked numerically: at x = 0.001 the expression is 0.66667.
lines: The standard limit is  lim(x → 0) ((1 + x)ⁿ − 1)/x = n.  Here n = 1/3.

recall.must_convey: That each half gives n = 1/3, so the sum is 2/3.
accept: each half gives one third so the answer is two thirds
n is one by three because it is a cube root
the limit is two by three
rendu halves one third ichi two thirds vasthundi
twice one third is two thirds

steps.why: Each half contributes n = 1/3 and the two are added. The answer is twice the exponent, which is why the square-root version of the same question gives 1.
common_mistakes: Giving 1/3, by using the standard limit only once.
Using n = 3 instead of n = 1/3; a cube root is the power one third.
steps.memory_tip: Both halves give the exponent 1/3, so the answer is 2 × 1/3.
